root_cause: The pinned openvino-genai/openvino-tokenizers wheels (2026.4.0.0) installed by the LLM accuracy test job link against libopenvino.so.2640, but the OpenVINO runtime build actually installed/on LD_LIBRARY_PATH in this merge-queue run does not provide that exact SONAME (a build/packaging or version-skew mismatch between the freshly built runtime and the pre-built GenAI wheel). This is unrelated to the PR under test, which only edits a docs .rst file, and the identical failure has now been recorded 5+ times across unrelated PRs since 2026-09-21, confirming it is an environment/packaging regression rather than a code defect introduced by this PR.
reproduction_steps: Not reproducible from this PR's diff (docs-only). To reproduce: build openvino runtime from the merge-queue commit, install openvino-genai==2026.4.0.0 and openvino-tokenizers==2026.4.0.0 from the pinned requirements, then run `python3 -m pytest tests/llm/accuracy_conformance.py -k CPU` and observe the ImportError for libopenvino.so.2640.
recommended_actions: Verify that the openvino-genai/openvino-tokenizers wheel versions pinned in the LLM test requirements match the SONAME (libopenvino.so.<version>) actually produced by the current runtime build
Check for a recent bump of the OpenVINO core version/SONAME without a corresponding openvino-genai wheel rebuild/republish
Ensure LD_LIBRARY_PATH / INSTALL_DIR wiring in the LLM accuracy test job points at the freshly built libopenvino.so rather than a stale one
Re-run once the packaging mismatch is fixed; this failure is unrelated to the current PR's docs change
prevention_strategies: Add a CI smoke check that imports openvino_genai right after installing the runtime + GenAI wheel in the LLM accuracy job, failing fast with a clear packaging-mismatch message instead of deep inside pytest collection. Pin openvino-genai/openvino-tokenizers wheel builds to the exact runtime SONAME via a compatibility check in the release pipeline.
historical_context: Same signature (a87e95431b0e8175) recorded 5 times since 2026-09-21T15:45:59Z, most recently at 2026-09-22T17:33:10Z, across unrelated PRs #38200, #38329, #38190 — confirms a persistent environment/packaging issue, not code introduced by this PR.
